title: First-degree AV block
summary: Every impulse reaches the ventricles, but the AV node conducts slowly, so the PR interval is long.

events.label: AV node
events.caption: The impulse enters the AV node, which conducts much more slowly than normal.
events.ecg: The PR segment is flat for longer than normal.

events.label: His bundle
events.caption: Eventually it emerges into the His bundle and spreads normally.
events.ecg: The PR interval is over 200 ms, here about 320.

events.label: Ventricles
events.caption: Every impulse still reaches the ventricles. The QRS is normal.
events.ecg: A narrow QRS follows every P wave: a delay, not a block.

teaching_points: First-degree AV block: every P wave is conducted, but the PR interval is longer than 200 ms (slides 28-30).
It represents prolonged AV conduction rather than a true block (slide 30) and does not by itself explain a bradycardia (slide 30).
The delay is usually in the AV node itself.
